title: Staged Mirror + Canary Orchestration for Zero-Egress Private Deployments
creator: Marco Chen
description: Enable safe, auditable rollouts for Private/VPC deployments with zero or minimal egress by combining staged artifact mirroring with a local canary orchestration flow. This PRD specifies networking constraints, offline image distribution requirements, upgrade choreography, health gating, and rollback criteria for environments that cannot reach external registries during normal operation.
goals: Define a repeatable process for distributing images and artifacts to isolated sites without direct internet egress.
Provide automated canary rollout orchestration that runs entirely within customer VPC or air-gapped networks.
Ensure upgrades can be validated at the binary and behavioral level before wide rollout, with fast rollback paths.
Offer clear acceptance tests and operator runbooks to reduce on-site manual steps to a minimum.
non_goals: Building a custom package distribution system from scratch (we will leverage existing mirror/registry tooling).
Solving hardware provisioning or non-software infrastructure concerns (power, racks).
Replacing customer's change management processes — this provides tooling to enable their approvals, not bypass them.
requirements: Minimal Egress Modes: Support three egress profiles — zero-egress (no outbound connections), restricted-egress (only to approved mirror endpoints), and staged-egress (temporary outbound allowed during maintenance windows).
Artifact Mirroring: Support mirror manifests for container images, Helm charts, and OS patches. Mirrors must be checksum-verified and signed with customer KMS/HSM-compatible signatures.
Staging API: Provide a CLI and API for operators to stage a release bundle into a target mirror, verify integrity, and schedule a canary window.

Local Registry Support: The private control plane must work with customer-provided registries (Harbor, Artifactory, private ECR) and fallback to a hosted proxy only for validation snapshots when allowed.

Canary Orchestration: Canary jobs must run inside the customer's VPC: deploy a configurable canary percentage (1–5%), perform smoke tests against workload-level and platform-level probes, collect metrics and traces to local observability endpoints.
Health Gating: Define automated gating rules (latency, error budget, model-output regressions for inference endpoints) with configurable thresholds and time windows.
Binary Provenance: All artifacts must carry provenance metadata (build id, signed digest, published-by) surfaced in console and CLI.

Rollback: Fast rollback path that reverts nodes to previous image and KV cache state within an operator-specified SLA (target: <10 minutes for canary, <60 minutes for rollback to prior stable for full cluster).
Upgrade Orchestration Offline Mode: All orchestration steps (image pull, validation, config update) must be executable without external DNS resolution when zero-egress is selected.
Operator Visibility: Console and CLI must show staged-mirror status, per-node artifact checksums, canary progress, and explicit logs of any egress performed during the operation.
Audit Logging: All actions must be audit-logged with immutable event ids and optional remote syslog export.
acceptance_criteria: Zero-Egress Validation: Run a full canary cycle in an air-gapped environment using only pre-mirrored artifacts. Success = canary pods become Ready, smoke tests pass, and no outbound connections are observed in network flow logs during the operation.

Checksum & Signature Verification: Mirrored artifacts fail deployment if signature or digest mismatch. Test case: tampered image in mirror is rejected with explicit audit event and operator-facing error.
Canary Gates Enforced: If health gates fail (latency > threshold or error rate spike), orchestration automatically pauses and triggers configured rollback with clear operator notifications.
Rollback Timing: Verify rollback completes within documented SLA in a test environment scaled to customer footprint (simulation acceptable).
Operator Runbook Execution: Guided runbook completes without manual artifact re-publishing steps; operator only confirms scheduled window and triggers approval.
Registry Interop: Successfully stage and deploy from at least two supported local registries (Harbor, private ECR) in customer-like networks.
Console Visibility: Console displays artifact provenance and per-node checksums for the deployed canary within 60s of canary start.
Audit Trails: Every mirror staging and canary event is present in audit logs with user, timestamp, artifact digest, and action outcome.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 — Internal validation: Deploy in Redwood-managed isolated cluster with simulated zero-egress mirrors (2 weeks).
Phase 2 — Pilot with 2 customers: coordinate with Customer Success, run full mirrored canaries during maintenance windows (4–6 weeks).
Phase 3 — GA: enable self-serve staging UI + CLI, documentation updates, and add to Private deployment offering (target release private-2026.03).
test_plan: Create synthetic air-gapped testbeds that block DNS and external IPs while providing a local mirror. Run multiple release bundles through staging API.
Simulate signature tampering and validate failure modes and audit records.
Load-test canary gating logic with injected latency and error spikes to ensure consistent pause+rollback behavior.
Measure rollback time across small, medium, and large cluster profiles and document deviations.
Run security review and penetration tests focused on mirror import, signature validation, and local registry credentials handling.
risks: Customers may have heterogeneous registry versions and authentication flows that increase integration surface area.
Operators could misconfigure scheduling windows, causing temporary downtime if rollback SLAs are not met.
Performance overhead of extra checksum/signature verification might increase upgrade time for very large clusters.
Edge cases around KV cache state restore during rollback could lead to model regression if not fully captured in tests.
open_questions: What is the minimal supported registry API surface (OCI manifest v2, v1 compat?) we commit to supporting at GA?
Do we require an on-prem sidecar agent to manage mirror ingestion, or can we fully rely on customer-run registry tooling?
What must the customer-provided mirror expose as a health endpoint for us to validate artifact completeness?
How will we surface signed attestations when the customer uses an HSM that disallows export of private keys?
